title: Choose the visual world for the invitation
question: The roll assigned The Sandwich Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sandwich Board
options.lineage: hand-lettered chalk A-frame outside a bistro
options.thesis: Tonight's special, written in chalk for one customer. Refuses the cream card with a script headline.
options.viewport: The board fills the phone edge to edge. TONIGHT ONLY across the top in yellow chalk, her name huge in white, 'dinner with me?' underneath, a chalk-drawn box to tick for yes. A chalk hand writes it in as she watches.
options.risk: Reads like a café menu if the lettering is timid or the palette stays white-on-black.

raised.raise: The headline draws as one continuous chalk stroke, never fades in.
Yes is drawn solid; the no option stays a dashed outline that never fills.
State is a chalk mark, not a color: a tick in a box, then a wipe and rewrite.
Three chalk faces and no more; rank is color and weight, not a size ladder.
The board owns the whole viewport, no page margins, no card shell.
One material for everything: the button, the date, and the time are chalk too.

options.label: The Tasting Menu
options.lineage: prix-fixe menu card at the table
options.thesis: The evening laid out as courses, and she is the first one.
options.viewport: A tall menu card: 'Menu for two', date on top, courses listed with a dotted leader; the last line is 'Yes' with a price of 'one smile'.
options.risk: The most familiar path; most runs in this category land on a printed card.

options.label: Neon in the Window
options.lineage: hand-bent neon sign in a restaurant window
options.thesis: One word lit in cobalt glass in a dark room, and it is her name.
options.viewport: Her name in continuous neon script, buzzing on. Below in smaller tube: 'dinner?' Tap the switch to light 'YES'.
options.case: A restaurant window sign is hers to recognize; loses on clarity because the details cannot read as neon.
options.risk: Glow effects tip into the dark-plus-neon default fast.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: Departure columns at one type size on goldenrod.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides with one departure row.
options.case: She has no reason to identify with an airline timetable; the invitation would need explaining.
options.kept: One lettering system, rank by weight and color.
options.risk: Reads as a design exercise, not a note from him.

options.label: Info-Noise Sleeve
options.thesis: Hostile brand noise with one shouting word.
options.viewport: Magenta target grid, her name shouting through hazard glyphs.
options.case: Hostile by design; wrong register for a love note and it hides the ask.

options.label: Sewing Pattern Tissue
options.thesis: Dashed cutting lines, one view committed in red.
options.viewport: Envelope front with views A, B, C.
options.case: Only lands if she sews; nothing in the brief says so.
options.kept: The committed choice renders solid, others dashed.
options.risk: Needs a hobby she may not have.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Frames on pins, orange tape flag where you stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated strip with three frames.
options.case: An editing bench is a work surface; the invitation is not a task.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.thesis: A scene made of glyph density in green phosphor.
options.viewport: Her name rendered as a rotating field of characters.
options.case: Terminal aesthetics read as his world, not hers.
options.risk: Hard to read on a phone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The e-invitation everyone ships: cream, script headline, a soft floral, one rounded Yes button.
canonCard.viewport: Centered card, script 'Will you have dinner with me?', a pink Yes button.
